newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO official calls for halting Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: PLO official calls for halting Hebron talks.

text.p: A senior Palestinian negotiator on Tuesday described negotiations on Israeli army redeployment in Hebron as a "mockery" and called for the talks to be halted.
"The current way of negotiating is not fruitful. This requires the halting of this mockery," Yasser Abed Rabbo told a news conference in the West Bank town of al-Bireh.

Abed Rabbo, who is also a minister in Yasser Arafat's administration, does not always reflect the views of the Palestinian president. There was no immediate word from Arafat about Abed Rabbo's comments.

The PLO has grown frustrated after a month of negotiations with Israel over a long overdue partial military pullout from Hebron. Israel agreed under a 1995 West Bank self-rule deal with the PLO to redeploy its troops from parts of the town in March.

But Israel's new right-wing government wants the accord signed by the previous Labour-led administration to be modified to bolster security for some 400 Jewish settlers living among more than 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron.
The PLO refuses to change the accord, saying it provides enough security for the settlers.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, who toured Hebron on Tuesday, reiterated that the PLO was to blame for the failure to reach an agreement so far on Hebron.
"I think the other side, the Palestinians, are not ready to come to a conclusion and to have an agreement about the redeployment in Hebron," Mordechai told reporters.

Abed Rabbo said the Palestinian leadership sent a letter to the U.S. government on Monday, demanding it pressure Israel to implement all provisions of the self-rule accord, including the Hebron redeployment.
He also called at the news conference for a summit of the parties involved in Middle East peace talks to re-emphasise a land-for-peace foundation of the peace process begun in 1991.

"The only way to avoid a comprehensive explosion is to call for a summit meeting attended by the PLO, Israel, the United States, Russia and the European Union in order to reiterate the basis for the peace process and commitment to signed deals," Abed Rabbo said.

"Without this, there will be an explosion because our differences with Israel is not over redeployment from a few streets in a Palestinian city. They are over the basis of the peace process and the signed agreements," he said.
He said Israel had dragged the talks into details of how many guns Palestinian police would carry and which streets in Hebron would be opened.
Israeli-PLO talks resumed under U.S. supervision in October following serious clashes between Israeli soldiers and Palestinian police in which 75 people from both sides died.
Israeli soldiers and Palestinian police resumed joint partols in the West Bank towns of Jenin and Jericho on Tuesday, more than one month after they were halted following the violence.
